annotation.title_clean: Is It Time to Consider EU Criminal Law Rules on Robotics?
annotation.title_en: Is It Time to Consider EU Criminal Law Rules on Robotics?
annotation.venue: Croatian Yearbook of European Law and Policy
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
EU Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
Commission Communication Artificial Intelligence for Europe
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed legal article by Croatian scholars asking whether the EU should adopt criminal law rules on robotics/AI. It reviews EU AI policy, including the Trustworthy AI guidelines, AI use in criminal proceedings, and AI as 'perpetrator' (autonomous vehicles, weapons), and argues the EU should regulate these areas and develop concepts of criminal liability for AI acts.
key_provisions_or_claims: EU-level criminal law rules on AI/robotics are needed and the EU's competence to adopt them is examined
AI in criminal investigation and interrogation threatens defendants' rights and requires EU principles and standards
Criminal liability for harms caused by autonomous systems (e.g., self-driving cars, autonomous weapons) is currently unclear
Criminal law faces a 'third revolution' requiring new concepts of liability for AI acts
Criminal liability of AI itself is not adopted in modern criminal law
